summary: Michela Clemente is a Tibetologist who studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and conducted postdoctoral research under Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015). She held a post as a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.

Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin (~1853–1857) under Giacomo Lignana and Mario Vallauri. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1870) and was a professor at the University of Naples Federico II (~1872–1910).
Michele Martin (born 1942) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and held a post at National Taiwan University.

Michelle Spuler (born 1971) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her PhD at the University of Queensland (~1996–2000). She taught in the Department of Religious Studies at Victoria University of Wellington and also taught at Colorado College.

Michiel de Vaan (born 1973) is a linguist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his doctorate under Alexander Lubotsky (~1997–2002) and held a post at Leiden University from ~2002 to 2014.

Michihiko Komine (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1964–1977). He served at Taisho University as an assistant (~1978–1983) and professor (~1993–2015), as professor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014), and led the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).

Michihiko Yajima (born 1958) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1992) and as professor at Tsurumi Women's University (attested 2003).

Michihiro Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He taught at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), and served as a librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005–2006).

Michiko Yusa (born 1951) is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She completed her doctorate under Raimon Panikkar at UC Santa Barbara (~1976–1983) and served as a professor of foreign languages at Western Washington University (~1983–2021).

Michio Kamikawa (1960–2021) specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University (~1980–1988) and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University from ~1998 to 2021.

Michio Yano (born 1944) is an Indologist and historian. He earned his doctorate at Kyoto University, where he also studied under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi, and studied at Brown University under David Pingree (~1974–1976). He was a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University (1973–2015).

Michitoshi Barada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi. He held appointments at Otani University (attested 1992), Eastern Institute (attested 2000), and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2000–2003, 2026).
Michiya Ito conducted graduate studies at Tohoku University, where he was attested in 1990. He also held posts at Tohoku University, attested in 1990 and from 2001 to 2004.

Michiyo Hoshi (born 1941) specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She has held posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa and as a researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 2003).

Midori Nishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006). She subsequently served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2010–2015).
Mieko Kajihara is an Indologist who studied under Michael Witzel (attested 1997) and earned a PhD from Harvard University in 2002.

Migmar Tsering (1956–1999) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He served as head of Sakya College (attested 1991–2003) and held posts at CIHTS (attested 1990) and the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2006).

Mihai Șora (1916–2023) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Bucharest under Mircea Eliade (~1934–1938), the University of Paris (~1939–1944), and the CNRS (~1945–1948). He worked at the State Publishing House for Literature and Arts (~1957–1969).

Mikaël Bauer specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned a PhD at Harvard University under Ryuichi Abe (attested 2010). He is Associate Professor at McGill University (attested 2026).

Mikel Burley works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Essex under J. M. Bernstein, studied under Jonardon Ganeri and Brian Carr, and completed a PhD under John Peacock at Bristol (2005). He is Associate Professor at Leeds (attested 2007–2020).
